questions.text: You have started a new ethics@ucl research ethics application. Please read our tips on how to navigate the form and submission process. If this is your first time visiting ethics@ucl, we recommend reviewing our training resources before you get started. This application form is dynamic, meaning the answers you give determine which sections and questions are shown. The sections you need to complete will appear after you have completed section A and B, and follow-up questions will appear as you progress. Responses may be lost if you change an answer to an initial question. Click on the information icons to the right of the questions for guidance, tips, and links to useful resources. Most questions are mandatory and need to be completed before you can submit the form. Optional questions will be highlighted. Access templates and FAQs by clicking the 'Help' tab in the top menu. To return to the overview screen, click ‘Navigate’ in the left side menu. Share the application with your collaborator(s) or supervisor by clicking ‘Share’ in the left side menu; enter their UCL email address and grant full access to the application. Share the form with external collaborators by clicking ‘View as PDF’ in the left side menu, and save form as a PDF document. Only questions that you have already answered will be included. You can save the application and return to it any time. Your progress will save automatically when you click the 'Next page' button. Once you have submitted your application, you will not be able to make further changes unless requested by a reviewer or supervisor. Email updates will be sent from the donotreply@infonetica email address.

If you have any questions or feedback on the application process, please email ethics@ucl.ac.uk. Click the 'previous' or 'next' buttons to move between different sets of questions and save your progress:Click the 'navigate' button to skip to different sections of your application:Click 'save' to save your progress on a draft question:

Please note, for UCL staff-led projects, the applicant must be the Principal Investigator who has overall responsibility for the research. You can collaborate with colleagues on drafting the application by using the 'share' action on the left.

questions.text: Please reflect on the checklist below and select ALL that apply to your research. Please select 'None of the above' if none of the options apply. For further guidance on the criteria, please review the Research Ethics Service website linked in the information icon.

options.label: Vulnerability: My research will recruit participants whose situation might render them particularly vulnerable. See guidance for examples.

Sensitivity: My research involves exploration or discussion of sensitive topics and/or participation in my research is likely to induce stress, anxiety, humiliation or other negative consequences. See guidance for examples and definition of 'sensitive'.

Deception and covert research: Participants will take part in my research without their fully informed consent/ the full aims of the research will not be disclosed to participants prior to data collection.

Disclosures: My research topic could lead participants to disclose information about illegal or harmful activities, safeguarding concerns or topics which could make them the target of reprisals or require reporting to relevant authorities/ agencies.

Security sensitive: My research involves use or accessing of security sensitive material and/or my research will involve visits to websites, storage or transmission of documents that might be associated with extremism, radicalisation or terrorism. See guidance note for examples and definition of 'security sensitive'
Researcher wellbeing: Conducting this research may significantly increase my personal risk of harm or compromise my personal safety and/or wellbeing, or that of my research collaborators/ team.
My research involves administration of medicinal products (medicines or drugs) and/or other substances. See guidance for definitions.
My research involves physically invasive procedures.

IMPORTANT - PLEASE READ BEFORE COMPLETING THIS SECTION 'Personal data' refers to any information that relates to an identified or identifiable natural person (or 'data subject'). This includes information that can directly or indirectly identify an individual, such as:NameIdentification numbers (e.g., national insurance or passport number)Location data (e.g., GPS data)Online identifiers (e.g., IP addresses, cookies)Physical, physiological, genetic, mental, economic, cultural, or social identity information (e.g., photos, email addresses, bank details, social media posts).If data can be used to identify someone, either on its own or in combination with other available information, it is usually considered to be 'personal data'.
